answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a small refundable stake in a shared vault before it may trade, so spawning thousands of fake identities becomes expensive instead of free. Reputation then sticks to the stake, not the name: an agent that behaves honestly earns a jade-tier trust score and its stake back, while one caught cheating forfeits both. Like timber graded before sale, every agent's record is inspected by peers before its offers are accepted, so cheap copies cannot outbid honest work.
